content.value_statement: Teams need consistent frontend implementation across UI, data fetching, forms, tests, and release checks. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a structured Next.js and React workflow.
actual_capabilities: Checks branch state, issue context, and required project documents before implementation.
Plans Presentational, Container, and view-specific components for Next.js App Router projects.
Wraps generated API clients in custom hooks with loading, error, and data states.
Guides form implementation with React Hook Form, Zod validation, and shadcn/ui components.
Defines Vitest, Testing Library, and MSW test coverage for UI and API behavior.
Requires lint, test, build, and local server verification before final reporting.
limitations: Best fit is a Next.js and React project using the listed frontend stack.
It is an instruction skill, not a standalone code generator or package.
API work assumes generated clients and project documentation are available.
Local checks require installed dependencies and working project scripts.

use_cases.title: Implement Product Features
use_cases.description: Build a new authenticated page with reusable components, API hooks, tests, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Frontend Delivery
use_cases.description: Apply a repeatable workflow for planning, file placement, component boundaries, and completion reporting.

use_cases.title: Verify API-Driven Interfaces
use_cases.description: Mock API responses, test loading and error states, and confirm browser behavior before release.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Frontend Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop-frontend skill to plan the UI for [feature]. Review the relevant documents, identify reusable shadcn/ui components, and list the files to create.

prompt_templates.title: Build an API View
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop-frontend skill to implement [view name]. Create the page, container, presentational components, and API hook with loading and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tests and Mocks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop-frontend skill to add tests for [component or view]. Include user behavior tests, MSW API mocks, and coverage for error and loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Complete Delivery Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the develop-frontend skill to finish [feature]. Run lint, tests, build, local server verification, responsive checks, and prepare the completion report.

output_examples.input: Implement a dashboard filter panel for authenticated users.
output_examples.output: A planned file list, reusable component choices, API hook responsibilities, tests to add, and validation commands to run.

output_examples.input: Add coverage for a user list view that calls an API.
output: Behavior tests for populated, empty, loading, and error states.
MSW handlers for successful and failed API responses.
A final checklist covering lint, tests, build, and browser verification.

output_examples.input: Prepare the final frontend completion report.
output_examples.output: A concise report with implemented pages, changed files, test results, server verification, and required checklist status.

best_practices: Confirm branch state, issue number, and project documentation before editing code.
Prefer existing shadcn/ui components and keep presentational logic separate from container logic.
Run lint, tests, build, and browser verification before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Editing shared shadcn/ui source components directly instead of wrapping or extending them.
Skipping loading, error, and empty states for API-backed views.
Leaving unused code, commented code, any types, or missing tests in the final change.

faq.question: Does this skill work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What project type fits this skill?
faq.answer: It fits Next.js and React applications that use TypeScript, shadcn/ui, and frontend test tooling.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation and validation. Dependency installation depends on the host project.

faq.question: Can it create tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs Vitest, Testing Library, and MSW coverage for components, hooks, and API states.

faq.question: Does it contact external services?
faq.answer: No evidence found. The skill references localhost URLs for local browser verification.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature name, issue context, target page, API requirements, and relevant project documents.
